findings.location: sections/concise/10-commentary.tex lines 332-333, unit 'A people on the march', first paragraph, last sentence (physical p. 9): 'The second, with Augustine, hears in both releases the work of mercy.'
findings.problem: Unchanged since iteration 0; the file is byte-identical to the sealed bytes. The sentence comes right after Cassiodorus's two releases: the world's pomps leaving the mind, and release a daemonum turba. A reader therefore takes 'both releases' to mean those two. The second reading's actual join is the study's: 'The release of the Exodus and the release of the debtor are both the work of mercy' (sections/30-debt-forgiven-from-the-heart.tex lines 237-240). The study grounds it on Augustine's 'no man is turned away in heart from this world, unless aided by the gift of the Divine mercy'. Compression lost that join, so the second reading's hearing of the Alleluia cannot be recovered here.
findings.required_result: Name the two releases the second reading joins: Israel's release from Egypt and the debtor's remission, both the work of mercy, since no one leaves Egypt in heart unless aided by the Divine mercy (Augustine). Do not credit Augustine with the join to the parable.

findings.location: sections/concise/10-commentary.tex lines 122-128, unit 'Who is the enemy, and what is the armour?', paragraph beginning 'The armour is armatura Dei' (physical p. 6): '... a figure of the spiritual war (In Ephesios III, PL 26, col. 543).'

findings.location: sections/concise/10-commentary.tex lines 34-37, unit 'A will none resists, and an adversary who asks', second paragraph (physical p. 5): 'Rupert of Deutz, citing the Introit's words in his treatise on God's omnipotence (he gives them as St Paul's), completes them ...'
findings.problem: The parenthesis credits Rupert with an attribution his words do not make. In De omnipotentia Dei 9 (PL 170, col. 461; tracked OCR patrologiaecursu0170mign_djvu.txt lines 33373-33374) he writes only 'Nonne scriptum est: Et non est qui possit resistere voluntati tuae?'. The '(Rom. ix)' after it is a printed chapter reference of the kind Migne's text supplies throughout the same passage ('(Gen. vi)', '(Job. ix.)', and the footnote marker '(41)' for Gregory). The chapter numbering it uses postdates Rupert, who died in 1129. In c. 10 (lines 33434-33436) he repeats the words with no attribution. Rom 9:19 is in any case a different sentence ('Voluntati enim ejus quis resistit?'). The Pauline reference is therefore the edition's, not Rupert's. The concise inherits the clause from the study (sections/20-armour-under-providence.tex lines 84-86) and from research/scope.md (Rupert entry, 'he cites it as Rom 9'). It is an aside that no reading depends on, which is why it does not block.
findings.required_result: Drop '(he gives them as St Paul's)', or say that Migne's edition refers the words to Rom 9. When the study and research/scope.md are next revised, make the same correction there.

summary: Cold review, iteration 1, of the concise study 61-twenty-first-after-pentecost-synthesis (synthesis.tex with sections/concise/01-90 and the shared generation record). Why it is repeated was verified, not trusted: scripts/_tooling.py hashes 19e041b8... at b9786e912^ and 86c302fc... at HEAD and on disk, and the commit adds only the proper-study-run-archive entries to GROUPS and REACHES. This packet's REVIEW_INPUTS equal iteration 0's review_inputs in every field, and all 16 sealed files re-hash equal on disk. No commit since e95bbc7f3 and no working-tree change touches the concise components, synthesis.tex, src/common or any study or research file. Research 3 and author-study 3 edited no content. REVIEW_SCOPE files: only generation-metadata.tex reaches this PDF. It moves the printed revision timestamp to 2026-10-15T16:27:39Z and adds the derive-homily contribution. check-generation-metadata --pdf and provenance-matches-run pass. All 32 receipt hashes in research/artifacts.json match disk. The production-review entries for derive-synthesis 0 and 1 and build-artifacts agree with what was reproduced here: 12 pages, PDF 3e066c1b..., aux 00c08850..., 9,384 pdftotext words. An independent pdflatex build in scratch was byte-identical to the build PDF and settled from the first pass. Its log has no warning or bad box. Its zref markers put inventory, overview and all four sense rows on p. 1, chronology on p. 2, themes on pp. 3-4 and commentary from p. 5. All 12 pages were inspected rendered, with no clipping, overflow or stray space. Each reading's answer was recovered from the concise prose before the study was opened. (1) God's government: Gregory's petition/permission (deficeret/proficeret), Thomas's will against power, and Chrysostom's enemy behind the persecutor. (2) The forgiven heart: Chrysostom's receiver revokes, Augustine's God calls back, Thomas's per ingratitudinem, and correction without rancour. (3) Time: Augustine's martyrs answered by long-suffering, Chrysostom's girded Passover march, and Thomas's reckoning from tribulation to judgment. Pages 5-11 develop and compare the reasoning beyond pp. 3-4. Page-2 lookup on the rendered table. Alleluia Ps 113:1 is found in two rows. One is the shared Psalter row, 'Before c. 165 B.C.'. The other is the retrospective Exodus row, Temple-relative (480th year, Vulgate; 440th, Septuagint), with the place phrase 'the years are reckoned from the founding of the Temple (3 Kgs 6:1)'. Offertory Job 1:1, 1:12, 2:6-7 is one composition row: place of writing unknown, story set in Hus, 'Probably sometime between the seventh and fifth centuries B.C.'. Epistle Eph 6:10-17 is a default row (Paul in chains, A.D. 58-63; 61) beside a labelled critical comparison (later disciple, c. A.D. 80-100). Each pairs left to right without crossing a column. All 11 rows are byte-identical to the study appendix's. The concise's English quotations come to 128 segments of three or more words. A script matched 122 of them to tracked texts: NPNF 6, 8, 10 and 13; the Oxford Moralia; Fromage; Schuster; Bellarmine; the ST English; Douay; verified.md. Five more were matched by reading, past OCR hyphenation, footnote markers and the Moralia's bracketed Latin. Only Alphonsus, who has no tracked text, was not matched. The Schuster and Fromage page loci check out against the OCR running heads. Latin loci read here in tracked OCR: Rupert, De div. off. XII.21 and De omnip. Dei 9-10 (PL 170); Durandus VI.138-139; Rabanus on Mt 18 (PL 107); Thomas, Super Eph. 6 lect. 3. The concise cites Rupert and Durandus only for elements their Masses share, and the parable at VI.139 without narrating its Sunday. SYN-001 to SYN-005 were re-verified against the study and records and are carried unchanged as advisories. SYN-006 is new. Limits: the concise's prose was not re-compared line by line with the study beyond these checks. Jerome PL 26, Hilary PL 9, PG 27, Cassiodorus, Honorius and Alphonsus were not reopened. Verdict: PASS, no blocking finding, six advisories.
